newsitem.title: UK: Natl power agrees extra coal deal with RJB.
newsitem.headline: Natl power agrees extra coal deal with RJB.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power Plc said it had agreed an extra two-year contract with RJB Mining for six million tonnes of coal.
National Power said the contract was in addition to existing supply deals which RJB inherited when it bought British Coal's mining activities in the England and North Wales in December 1994.
National Power said up to three million tonnes of coal would be supplied over the next 12 months with the balance in the second year of the contract.
It said discussions on arrangements to succeed contracts inherited by RJB from British Coal were continuing.
The extra coal will mainly be supplied to National Power's Drax coal-fired power station in north east England.
"We firmly believe that this contract...demonstrates National Power's longer-term commitment to coal," RJB Mining chief executive Richard Budge said in a statement.

Britain's opposition Labour party, widely expected to win power in a general election on May 1, is often viewed by political observers as more favourable to coal generation than the rival Conservative party, which privatised the industry after breaking a long strike by miners in the 1980s. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
